task.approach: Voices approach: this slice is a roster, a tip sheet, not your assignment — every citizen with a page on the record, one line each. You pick whose own words carry the day, and why. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

plan.focus: The impact of the A's success on Uptown residents and businesses
plan.closeQuestion: How can the community ensure that the positive energy around the A's success is sustained and benefits the neighborhood in the long term?

sources.name: Alicia Hernandez
sources.quote: To be honest, the A's haven't really affected my business or daily life that much. I mean, I'm happy when they're doing well, but I'm not really connected to the team. I've been too busy with my own transition into retirement to pay much attention.

sources.name: Mariana Kapoor
sources.quote: To be honest, I don't really know much about the A's success. I mean, I know they're the A's and they play baseball, but I haven't really been following how they're doing this season. My mom talks about the neighborhood and how people are feeling, and sometimes we see A's players around Chinatown, like Desmond Morton, he's a left fielder and my friend Eshe's mom loves watching him play. But I don't really know how the team's doing right now or how it affects our neighborhood. I just know that when we had that parade with the kids on our block, it felt like everyone was happy and having fun, and that's what stuck with me.

sources.name: Pilar Ramirez
sources.quote: To be honest, I'm not really sure how the community can benefit from the A's success. I mean, I love the team, but I've never really thought about it directly. I know my husband Vincent and I have argued about the A's and the Oaks, but that's more about our loyalty and curiosity than how it affects the community.
